significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that changing a decoded mechanistic variable predicts a downstream response matching an independently specified scientific curve in magnitude and sign, while most merely decodable variables have low "mechanistic fidelity"—"the fraction of predicted counterfactual variance realized." This establishes both a behavioral counterfactual regularity and an internal causal mechanism, constraining which representations may explain model outputs rather than merely repeating the existence-style probing evidence whose limitations motivate Hewitt and Liang (2019); a false result in which most concepts exhibit the predicted response would instead support widespread causal use of decoded scientific variables. The conclusion is somewhat underdetermined because "a minority of decodable scientific concepts pass" lacks a defined population and pass threshold, but the response-curve coupling itself distinguishes true and false states. In the topic-substitution check, the broad topic alone would not earn this score: the extra weight comes specifically from requiring quantitative agreement between representation edits and scientific counterfactual laws.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "mechanistic fidelity" score, a diagnostic comparing realized with scientifically predicted counterfactual variance; it can audit whether a decoded concept is causally used before researchers rely on mechanistic claims, although it is post hoc with respect to the model responses used to compute it. After re-extraction on a new model, the proposal supplies a standard for looking but does not predict that model's fidelity value or response parameters, apart from the imprecise expectation that only a minority will pass. The hypothesis asserts scope "across scientific foundation models" and names molecular, materials, protein, and physics settings, but its most direct downstream users are interpretability researchers and model auditors rather than scientists receiving a transferable scientific law or deployment-ready control. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the reusable score and theory-matched edit-response relation, rather than scientific-model interpretability in general, provide the modest reach above a bare probing claim.
